about: The Bosca family has made wine and amaro in Canelli, in the heart of Piedmont’s Moscato country, since 1820. The business is led today by Giovanni Bosca and Mariacristina Castelletta with their sons Giulio and Guglielmo, the family’s eighth generation of winemakers. Cardamaro was created in the 1950s by an ancestor, Rachele Torlasco Bosca, a scholar and herbalist who was fascinated by the properties of the cardoon, the thistle-like cousin of the artichoke that is grown across the region.

It is a vino amaro, a bitter aromatised wine rather than a spirit-based amaro. Cardoon, blessed (St. Benedict’s) thistle and ginger are each macerated separately in neutral alcohol, then blended with Piedmontese Moscato wine and sugar; Bosca’s herbalists later expanded the recipe with twenty-three further botanicals. The blend rests at least six months in oak before bottling at 17% alcohol, low enough that it should be kept in the refrigerator once opened, like a wine.

Cardoon and thistle lead, with gentle spice behind and the soft texture of its wine base. Like any wine-based aperitif, it is best fresh. Its importer suggests it in place of sweet vermouth, or even whiskey, in lighter cocktails, lengthened with cider or ginger ale, or poured beside robust soft and hard cheeses at the end of a meal.
facts: Cardoon, blessed thistle and ginger, plus 23 others
